items.title: The pages were on GitHub the whole time, and the gate was watching the wrong folder
items.summary: Gate 4 accepted 168 rows into the developer manual -- 157 command pages restamped with this run's lineage, seven that gained real content from a promoted harvest, zero validation findings and zero rollbacks -- with the catalog holding at 241 command keys matched to 241 parsed contracts and zero fallback rows. The interesting part was a side finding. The manual's own section files link to 22 command pages that the development branch does not have, and the first reading of that was that 22 pages had never been written. Measuring the other trees inverted it: 19 of them have been on the published branch and in the staging tree since 18 July, and only three -- USER, BUILDVECTORS and VDISK -- exist nowhere at all. Development tracks 164 of 183 command pages, none of its 28 section files, and none of its four appendices; 803 files live upstream that this branch has never carried. So the published manual is internally complete on the branch it was published to, and every gate in the flush had been measuring a publication its own branch does not track. The check written for exactly that defect was scoped, a month ago, to the one directory where the problem had already been fixed, and has printed PASS on every commit since. Two other instruments were repaired in the same pass: the website's progress authority now names the fields it fails on instead of returning a bare verdict, and on its first real run that naming caught this run about to publish publication_authorized as true for a run that had not reached its publication gate. A boolean would have been answered by re-deriving, and the stale value would have gone to the authority six freshness contracts resolve against.

items.title: The site published before its own cover page caught up
items.summary: Release 145 went live with the catalog at 241 command keys matched to 241 parsed contracts, zero fallback rows, and a HELP store that had just shed a duplicated usage-contract family: 29,700 line rows down to 18,566, artifacts and sections falling 14,844 to 10,587 apiece, contract drift reaching zero. Then the banner on all 151 published pages was found still reading 'Full-stack docs reconciled 2026-09-02'. Six freshness contracts had passed throughout, because every one of them compares a page against an authority file, and that authority was typed by hand and had not been regenerated. The pages agreed with the authority and the authority agreed with itself. The fix was to give it a generator, which is the one thing the two artifacts sitting beside it already had.

items.title: Four acceptance plans, three discarded, every one of them green
items.summary: A manual acceptance ran four times before it was allowed to land. Three plans were built and thrown away, and all four reported PASS_PLAN_ONLY with zero findings. The discarded ones would have joined text across a field boundary mid-word, turning 'not the command name' into 'not the comm and name', and welded list items into sentences on eight pages. The measurement in use, a fragment count, fell for a wrong join exactly as it fell for a right one. What caught them was diffing every staged page against its accepted counterpart and refusing to leave any difference unexplained.

items.title: The accepted manual had never been in version control
items.summary: The command reference the site links to was accepted in July and tracked by git for the first time on 2026-09-02: all 165 pages landed as new files. The reader page was tracked; the pages it links to were not, so nothing looked wrong from either end. Every acceptance in that window wrote into files git could not see, which meant no acceptance could be reviewed as a diff. A link-integrity gate now asserts that every page the accepted index links to exists and is tracked, and 47 unreferenced orphan pages were removed.

items.title: The documentation stack reaches its owner gate
items.summary: The current documentation pass closed its development checks with 239 command keys matched to 239 parsed contracts, no fallback command rows, 670 reachable HELP topics, and a new 25-section manual candidate. The local website now carries those measurements, while publication remains deliberately held at the owner gate.

items.title: A whole database lives inside another database
items.summary: The workbench can inspect a memo that carries a complete MINIDB container and hydrate its tables and native indexes into RAM. The demonstrated sample rebuilt thirteen tables and eleven index containers from the memo payload; recursive and nested multi-workspace management remains clearly labeled Alpha work.

items.title: One UI definition, four early consumers
items.summary: The application UI definition lane now has a DBF/FPT design-table contract and early wxWidgets, Tk, HTML, and character-cell consumers. It is featured as Alpha: useful implementation exists, while the proposed text commands and remaining native proof are still open.

items.title: Visual FoxPro forms and menus, read directly
items.summary: A form or menu saved by Visual FoxPro is a database table with a memo sidecar, so the reader that opens a table opens those too. Reading real ones settled what any converter would have to handle: one form carried twenty-four distinct control classes, and the columns of a grid turned out to have no records at all -- they exist only as a count kept on the parent, so walking the records alone loses every label inside the grid. The menu language proved to be ordinary text that FoxPro itself writes out, which means a menu and the program generated from it are a matched pair a future generator can be checked against rather than argued about.

items.title: The Python binding becomes its own product
items.summary: pydottalk was being built as a switch of the engine build, so producing a four-source module also compiled the entire command-line runtime and the terminal UI library it never referenced. It now builds standalone against the same engine sources, with its own build presets and its own lifecycle charter.

items.title: The maintenance console gets a light theme
items.summary: Every colour moved behind theme variables, so no literal value can outlive a theme change. Contrast was measured rather than eyeballed, and the light default now matches the website's own preference key instead of inventing a second one.

items.title: Five guards that could not fail
items.summary: Five checks across the toolchain returned the same answer for "nothing is wrong" and "nothing was examined", and each had been passing for months. Every one now judges against a declared truth, and each new test was proven able to fail before it was trusted.

items.title: Record locking, re-proven from the ground up
items.summary: A locale installed for console text encoding also changed number formatting, which corrupted the owner identifier written into lock sidecars. A lock could therefore be reclaimed while its owner was still running. Fixed at the cause, made fail-closed, and covered by the first test the lock subsystem has ever had.

items.title: Workspace write-back closed to green
items.summary: The write-back path now refuses a collision without writing anything, replaces only on explicit confirmation, and keeps a recoverable backup. Each assertion was checked for its ability to fail before the suite was believed.

items.title: Memo sidecar carriage and the descend probe
items.summary: Workspaces carried inside memo objects gained a verified sidecar path, and a probe for descending into nested container state.

items.title: Lean entry site deployed, licence settled
items.summary: A minimal entry site went live on its own domain, and the licence question that had been deferred through several releases was answered.

items.title: CNX indexes on x64 tables warn rather than refuse
items.summary: Opening a CNX index against an x64 table used to be refused outright. It now warns and proceeds where the combination is safe, with the boundary demonstrated rather than assumed.

items.title: External course intake, and a gateway that aborts cleanly
items.summary: An external learning-management intake lane was accepted, and the local gateway now handles aborted requests without leaving the surface in a half-served state.

items.title: Two lifecycle vocabularies merged into one
items.summary: The project had been carrying two names for the same product lifecycle. One was retired and its material merged, so there is a single vocabulary for how work is chartered and closed.
